title: Oil price shocks as IV for inflation on investment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
**Instrumental Variables (IV)** using oil price shocks as an instrument for inflation. The method addresses endogeneity between inflation and investment by exploiting exogenous variation in oil prices. Key assumptions: (1) Relevance - oil price changes significantly predict inflation (first stage), (2) Exclusion restriction - oil prices only affect investment through inflation (questionable since oil is a key input cost), (3) Exogeneity - oil price shocks are uncorrelated with unobserved determinants of investment.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(AER)
library(stargazer)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s24_data.csv")

# Check data structure
cat("Data dimensions:", dim(data), "\n")
cat("Summary statistics:\n")
print(summary(data))

# First Stage: Regress inflation on oil price shock + controls
first_stage <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = data)
cat("\n=== FIRST STAGE RESULTS ===\n")
print(summary(first_stage))

# Check instrument relevance (F-statistic should be > 10)
first_stage_f <- summary(first_stage)$fstatistic[1]
cat("\nFirst-stage F-statistic:", round(first_stage_f, 3))
if(first_stage_f > 10) {
  cat(" - STRONG INSTRUMENT\n")
} else {
  cat(" - WEAK INSTRUMENT WARNING\n")
}

# OLS (biased) estimation for comparison
ols_model <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = data)
cat("\n=== OLS RESULTS (for comparison) ===\n")
print(summary(ols_model))

# IV estimation using 2SLS
iv_model <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = data)
cat("\n=== IV/2SLS RESULTS ===\n")
print(summary(iv_model))

# Extract key coefficient
iv_coef <- coef(iv_model)["x"]
iv_se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(iv_model)))["x"]
cat("\n=== MAIN RESULT ===\n")
cat("IV coefficient on inflation:", round(iv_coef, 4), "\n")
cat("Standard error:", round(iv_se, 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(iv_coef - 1.96*iv_se, 4), ",", round(iv_coef + 1.96*iv_se, 4), "]\n")

# Robustness checks
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")

# 1. Hausman test for endogeneity
hausman_test <- summary(iv_model, diagnostics = TRUE)
cat("Hausman test p-value:", round(hausman_test$diagnostics["Wu-Hausman", "p-value"], 4), "\n")

# 2. Sargan test (would need overidentification - skip for single instrument)
cat("Note: Sargan test requires overidentification (multiple instruments)\n")

# 3. Reduced form (oil shock directly on investment)
reduced_form <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = data)
rf_coef <- coef(reduced_form)["z"]
cat("Reduced form coefficient (oil shock on investment):", round(rf_coef, 4), "\n")

# 4. Alternative specification without controls
iv_no_controls <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = data)
iv_coef_alt <- coef(iv_no_controls)["x"]
cat("IV coefficient without controls:", round(iv_coef_alt, 4), "\n")

# 5. Check for weak instrument bias (Stock-Yogo critical values)
cat("\nStock-Yogo 10% maximal IV size critical value: 16.38")
cat("\nOur F-statistic:", round(first_stage_f, 3))
if(first_stage_f > 16.38) {
  cat(" - PASSES weak instrument test\n")
} else {
  cat(" - FAILS weak instrument test\n")
}

# Final summary
cat("\n=== FINAL SUMMARY ===\n")
cat("OLS coefficient:", round(coef(ols_model)["x"], 4), "\n")
cat("IV coefficient:", round(iv_coef, 4), "\n")
cat("Difference suggests bias of:", round(coef(ols_model)["x"] - iv_coef, 4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
**Expected sign: Negative** - Higher inflation should reduce real investment as it increases uncertainty and real borrowing costs. **Expected magnitude: -0.3 to -0.8** - A 1 percentage point increase in inflation reduces log investment by 30-80 basis points. The IV estimate should be larger in absolute value than OLS if there's attenuation bias from measurement error, or smaller if simultaneity bias dominates (investment booms coinciding with inflationary periods). The exclusion restriction concern suggests the IV estimate may be biased toward finding stronger negative effects since oil shocks directly hurt investment through input costs.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: IV/2SLS — oil price instrument; must defend exclusion restriction; test overidentification if multiple instruments
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Inflation reduces investment; exclusion restriction requires sector-level controls
